title: Princeton Folio — Humanities Block Quote
description: A graduate humanities seminar template anchored by a single centered block quotation — wide vertical margins, small-caps course code, and em-dash attribution enforce scholarly restraint over visual decoration.
philosophy: This template exists for the room where the text is the argument. It refuses bullet points, gradient fills, and any layout element that competes with the primacy of the quoted passage. Designed for Socratic seminar settings where instructor and students read together from a projected handout, it treats body serif typography as the sole expressive instrument. The single oxblood accent on the course code is not decoration — it is a colophon, marking institutional context without editorial intrusion.
goodFor: Graduate seminar close-reading sessions centered on a single passage
Critical theory or philosophy lectures projecting primary source excerpts
Courses requiring on-screen attribution with formal em-dash citation style
Instructors replicating the aesthetic of Princeton or Yale seminar handouts
avoidFor: Multi-point argument slides with nested bullet hierarchies
Brand launches or pitch decks requiring strong visual identity
STEM lectures where equations and figures must coexist with prose
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the title page of a Princeton graduate seminar packet — quiet institutional authority earned entirely through typographic scale contrast and white space. The course code is a colophon, the title a formal pronouncement, the attribution a scholarly bow; each element is distinct in weight and spacing, never competing. Avoid any texture, gradient, icon, or illustrative element; compositional drama arrives through restraint alone.

  <text x="960" y="630" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="108" font-weight="400" font-style="italic" fill="#1e1c1a" letter-spacing="-2">of the Quoted Passage</text>

examples.layoutNotes: Single centered column occupying the middle third of the slide width, flanked by generous left and right white space. A thin full-width horizontal rule separates a small-caps course code at top from the large centered deck title below. A secondary em-dash attribution or semester line sits one step smaller beneath the title. Folio number anchors bottom-center; no header band, no sidebar elements.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a page torn from a Princeton seminar reader and projected onto a wall — hushed, unadorned, and completely confident in the weight of the words alone. Compositional rhythm is slow and vertical: the eye enters through the small-caps colophon, descends into the wide embrace of the block quote, and rests on the em-dash attribution below. There is no visual noise, no competing layer — only degrees of textual presence. Avoid anything that reads as designed in the commercial sense: no background texture, no illustrative motif, no accent shape that draws attention away from the passage itself.
examples.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#f5f0e6"/>

  <!-- Colophon: course code, flush-left at top margin -->
  <text x="120" y="92" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="20" fill="#7d2a2a" letter-spacing="6" font-variant="small-caps" font-weight="500">
    HUM 216 · INTERPRETING THE ANCIENT WORLD · SPRING SEMINAR VII
  </text>

  <!-- Faint hairline beneath colophon, almost invisible, just anchoring the margin -->
  <line x1="120" y1="112" x2="260" y2="112" stroke="#7a7468" stroke-width="0.75" opacity="0.55"/>

  <!-- Block quotation, cols 3–10 (x ≈ 373 to 1253) -->
  <!-- Opening quotation mark, oversized, sits slightly left of the block's left edge -->
  <text x="328" y="342" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="132" fill="#1e1c1a" font-style="italic" font-weight="400">“</text>

  <!-- The passage itself — roman serif, italic on the operative phrase -->
  <g font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" fill="#1e1c1a" font-size="40" font-weight="400">
    <text x="373" y="360" letter-spacing="-0.2">
      <tspan>We are discussing no small matter, but </tspan><tspan font-style="italic">how we ought</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="373" y="422" letter-spacing="-0.2">
      <tspan font-style="italic">to live</tspan><tspan>. And the question, once posed, will not release</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="373" y="484" letter-spacing="-0.2">
      us easily — for the examined life is not a possession one
    </text>
    <text x="373" y="546" letter-spacing="-0.2">
      acquires and thereafter holds, but a labor renewed each
    </text>
    <text x="373" y="608" letter-spacing="-0.2">
      morning against the drift of custom. What the interlocutor
    </text>
    <text x="373" y="670" letter-spacing="-0.2">
      seeks is not assent but the slower courtesy of <tspan font-style="italic">thought</tspan>,
    </text>
    <text x="373" y="732" letter-spacing="-0.2">
      which arrives, if at all, only after the argument has been
    </text>
    <text x="373" y="794" letter-spacing="-0.2">
      allowed to wound the one who carries it.”
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- Em-dash attribution, flush-right beneath closing quote, half-line gap -->
  <text x="1253" y="870" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="26" fill="#1e1c1a" text-anchor="end" font-style="italic" font-weight="400">
    — after Plato, Republic, 352d (trans. reading copy)
  </text>
  <text x="1253" y="904" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="22" fill="#7a7468" text-anchor="end" font-weight="400">
    Week Seven · Assigned Passage · to be read aloud
  </text>

  <!-- Page number, bottom-center, reduced scale, receding -->
  <text x="960" y="1012" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="18" fill="#7a7468" text-anchor="middle" letter-spacing="3" font-variant="small-caps">
    — 23 —
  </text>
</svg>
examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; block quotation occupies cols 3–10, indented symmetrically from both sides to signal its quoted status. Top and bottom margins are wide and equal — roughly 16–18% of slide height — creating monastic vertical breathing. Course code in small-caps sits flush-left at the very top edge within the outer margin column (col 1–2), serving as a colophon rather than a header. Em-dash attribution is set flush-right below the closing quotation mark, separated by a half-line gap; no rule, no box. Page number, if present, lives bottom-center in a reduced scale, receding from the main reading axis.
